topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, frames the scope of the cancer lecture series, and outlines the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Conceptual frameworks and epidemiological evidence for cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer, examining the interplay between endogenous mutations, bad luck, inherited genetics, and environmental risks substantiated by geographical epidemiology.

topics.label: Mechanisms of specific carcinogens and tumour promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents to explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms of carcinogenesis, tissue specificity, and the distinction between tumour initiation and promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for determining carcinogenicity and exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and prove their links to cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk–benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a final summary of environmental cancer risks and the daily balance of risks versus benefits.
